elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Contractor to indemnify Company for such claims but contains no duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Contractor must indemnify Company against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or coverage for Contractor's breach of law is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The indemnity is limited to intellectual-property claims and does not cover Contractor's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or data-breach trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no indemnity for a data breach caused by Contractor.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no indemnity for Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: All required Vendor defense obligations must protect Customer's affiliates as well as Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no defense duty and no reference to Company's affiliates.

elements.element: All required Vendor indemnity obligations must protect Customer's affiliates as well as Customer.
elements.evidence: The indemnity protects only Company; affiliates are not identified as indemnitees.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnified party to provide notice of covered claims.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no notice procedure.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense and settlement of covered claims.
elements.evidence: The clause does not allocate control of defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, with no other indemnity triggers.
elements.evidence: The rendered language imposes no indemnity obligation on Company, so there is no broader Customer indemnity requiring restriction.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Contractor must indemnify Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate an intellectual-property right.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims to the extent arising from Customer's modification of the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The indemnity excludes claims to the extent arising from modification of the Works by Company.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims to the extent arising from Customer's combination of the deliverables with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnity excludes claims arising from Company's combination of the Works with items not supplied by Contractor.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims to the extent arising from Vendor's compliance with specifications furnished by Customer.
elements.evidence: The indemnity excludes claims arising from Contractor's compliance with specifications furnished by Company.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to procure Customer's right to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: Contractor may procure for Company the right to continue using the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to modify the affected item so that it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Contractor may modify the affected item so that it is non-infringing.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing item.
elements.evidence: Contractor may replace the affected item so that it is non-infringing.

elements.element: Vendor must refund the fees paid for the affected item if procurement, modification, and replacement are not reasonably available.
elements.evidence: If none of the other remedies is reasonably available, Contractor must refund the fees paid for the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor may select among procurement, modification, and replacement before the conditional refund remedy applies.
elements.evidence: The remedies are available at Contractor's option, with refund required only when none is reasonably available.

elements.element: Vendor's IP-indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times the annual fees rather than the ordinary liability cap.
elements.evidence: Notwithstanding Section 7(a), Contractor's liability under the indemnity paragraph is capped at three times the annual fees paid under the Agreement.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the fallback IP indemnity, exclusions, remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap. It does not meet the preferred position because it omits a defense duty, affiliate protection, non-IP indemnity triggers, and indemnification procedures. The change is not strictly minimal because it unnecessarily relocates the existing IP warranty. Drafting quality is reduced by the reference to an unlabeled 'Section 7(d)' and the heading's continued reference to indemnification of Contractor, although the inserted indemnity remains sufficiently identifiable and unrelated commercial terms remain operative.
